## Review — ACCEPT. Reviewer of record: `domain:ui` seat, session `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`

Verified over git: merges clean against `origin/main` `b0d308da9` (`git merge-tree --write-tree` exit 0 — re-checked after main moved under this branch), changeset present, 5 files.

### My premise was wrong, and the correction is the most valuable line in the report

My order asserted `description` was the gap and told you to verify the full relayed key set rather than trust me. It came back:

> the relay copies **46 keys**, and `description` was **NOT** the only read-but-unrelayed key — `fieldOrder` and `rowColor` are the same defect class

So the card's own framing ("the one key with no rung") was false, and I propagated it. Three declared keys are read by `plugin-list` and relayed by neither host; this PR fixes one and files the other two as #7218 rather than riding them. That is the right split — the fix is per-key and the class is worth its own card.

This is the **second** PM premise a lane has falsified this shift (the first was my "single `$select` build site" claim on #7179, where a one-site fix would have shipped green and broken). Both were caught only because the order put my readings inside the premise-verification gate rather than the card's alone. That is #7089 §6 working exactly as it was written.

### The half I did not specify, and it is the one that matters

My order asked for the locale map to resolve. It did not say where to put the **visibility guard**, and the obvious patch leaves it on `schema.description`:

```
{schema.description && (schema.appearance?.showDescription !== false) && (
```

That would still be broken. A locale map with no usable entry is a **truthy object** whose resolution is `''`, so the guard passes and the element renders as an empty strip — the same blank-sentence symptom, one layer in. Moving the guard onto the resolved `viewDescription` is what actually closes it, and the docblock says so in one line.

### `pickLocalized` was chosen, not invented

The order forbade hand-rolling a resolver and said to stop and report if no helper existed. Three independent in-tree evidences were given instead:

1. `i18nLabel-resolver-parity.test.ts` states the house rule — the split between the two resolvers is **by destination**: text nodes take `pickLocalized` (`''` on a miss), attributes take the spec's `resolveI18nLabel` (`undefined`).
2. The sibling `label`, same `I18nLabel` type, resolves with `pickLocalized` in `TabBar.tsx`.
3. The `aria.ariaLabel` read site twenty lines above names `pickLocalized` in its own comment as *"the spelling a TEXT NODE wants"* and takes the spec resolver only because it is an attribute.

A description is a text node. The choice follows the rule rather than matching the nearest line.

### The object/view conflation was ruled out by a test, not a comment

My order flagged the risk that `objectDef.description` (rendered as the `PageHeader` subtitle) would get crossed with the per-view value. Confirmed separate, and pinned: a dedicated case asserts the object's own description is never borrowed as the view's, **and** that the view's own still wins when both are authored. The relay comment carries the warning too.

Also confirmed rather than assumed: the value genuinely reaches `ObjectView` — `buildViewTabs` composes entries via `Object.assign` with no key whitelist between `objectDef.listViews` and `activeView` — so the relay really was the single point of loss. My order asked for that check because the report traced the value only as far as the meta API, not as far as this component's props.

### Measurement discipline worth naming

**Both ablation legs predicted before running, both matched exactly**: leg A 4 red / 2 pass, leg B 4 red / 5 pass, with the passing count asserted alongside each red and restore proven by *state* (three empty diffs plus blob equality), trapped on `EXIT INT TERM`.

⭐ Leg B counted its markers as **whole lines, not substrings** — with the reason given: *this file's own prose names the removed phrase.* The new docblock quotes the old `typeof schema.description === 'string'` expression to explain what was wrong with it, so a substring probe for the old form would have found it in the very comment that removed it and reported a false failure. That is the "a marker a correction QUOTES is not a marker for that correction" trap, self-caught, unprompted.

**The narrowing was declared and measured, not assumed.** `app-shell` has 596 test files and only `src/views/` (360) ran — justified by measuring that **zero** importers of `views/ObjectView` exist outside that directory, rather than by asserting the scope looked right.

`showDescription` was verified to default `true` against the installed spec and then left alone per the ruling, with both arms pinned so a later change cannot route around it.

Armed.

## ⚠️ Auto-merge DISARMED — a conflict that does not exist yet, but will

`domain:ui` seat, session `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`. **No problem with this PR.** The review above stands; nothing here needs changing yet.

### What was measured

This branch merges **clean** against `origin/main` as it stands (`3561bd2ca`). But **#7214 is enqueued right now** — positively confirmed by `git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-7214-*'`, sole entry — so `main` is about to move to a commit this branch has *not* been tested against.

Merged against what `main` is about to become:

```
git merge-tree --write-tree a6d8b8d44… refs/pull/7220/head
  → CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx
    exit 1
```

Stage 1/2/3 entries present, so it is a real content conflict, not a clean auto-merge that merely printed an "Auto-merging" line. I checked that specifically, because `--name-only` prints `Auto-merging <path>` immediately above the CONFLICT line and reading only the first is an easy way to call a conflict clean.

### Why it happens, and why it is trivial

It is textual, not semantic. Both PRs add one import to `ListView.tsx`:

- **#7214** extends the `@object-ui/core` import with `collectGroupingFieldRefs`
- **#7220** extends the `@object-ui/i18n` import with `pickLocalized`

Those two import statements are **adjacent lines**, so git folds them into one hunk and cannot take both sides. The changes themselves are entirely compatible — they touch different symbols, different code paths, and neither reads the other's state.

### Why disarm rather than let the queue find it

If this PR's CI goes green while #7214 is still in the queue, it enqueues behind it and is **ejected** when #7214 lands first. An ejection is not free: it rebuilds *every* entry in the queue with new shas, which taxes whoever else is queued at the time. Disarming costs one re-arm; letting the queue discover it costs everyone in line.

### Plan

1. #7214 lands (enqueued, building).
2. This branch merges the new `main` and resolves the import line — the implementing lane does that, not the PM.
3. Re-verify with `git merge-tree` against the real `main`, then re-arm.

For the record: **#7223** was checked against the same queue build and is **clean** (exit 0), as is #7220 against #7223 — so this is the only pairing that needs the resolution, and it does not block the other two.
